To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a user simulation model that randomly explores the dialog state space with certain constraints is suitable for learning a dialog strategy from a small number of dialog training examples, because it can achieve similar performance to a more complex user simulation model that aims to simulate realistic user behaviors in terms of dialog state transitions, and because a user simulation model with constraints is easier and more flexible to implement and can achieve better performance than a model without constraints.
a user simulation model that aims to explore more dialog states with certain constraints is suitable for developing training corpora for learning dialog strategies using MDPs.

(a) with sparse training data (i.e., less than 1000 dialogues) and a limited amount of time (i.e., 10 minutes per dialogue) for each user simulation, a user simulator that aims to randomly and efficiently explore more dialog state space is a better choice than a simulator that tries to simulate more realistic users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what kind of user model is appropriate for the task of automatically learning dialog strategies.
how to use a small amount of human annotated training data to learn dialog strategies for a dialog system.
the question of whether the training data should be as realistic as possible, or if it is more important to have a wide variety of dialog states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a simple random exploration model with certain constraints can be a reasonable choice for training data generation.
, for the purpose of training dialog strategy models with MDPs, a simple model is better than a sophisticated model.
a user simulation model that aims to explore more dialog state space, with certain constraints, performs at the same level as a more complex model, and is easier to train.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple and efficient user simulator can be used to train a good dialog strategy model.
a simple user simulation model is more suitable for developing a small training corpus for dialog strategy learning than a sophisticated one.
the more realistic the user simulation model is, the more training data is needed for it to perform better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the training data is the key to the performance of a user model.

the user model does not need to be too realistic in order to learn a good dialog strategy, which may have a positive impact on reducing the cost of training corpus development for dialog strategy learning.
the choice of user model should be based on how the training corpus will be used.
